You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

If by “rich visitor” you mean visitors who spent the most money (in `visit.Total_spent`), you can get their details like this:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent_all_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_spent_all_visits DESC;
```

If you want only the single richest visitor:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent_all_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_spent_all_visits DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

Do you mean “rich” as **highest total spent**, **highest membership level**, or **spent the most on a single visit**?
I mean the visitor who bought the most tickets.

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

If you want *all* visitors tied for most tickets:

```sql
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT visitor_ID, SUM(Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
  FROM visit
  GROUP BY visitor_ID
),
mx AS (
  SELECT MAX(total_tickets) AS max_tickets FROM totals
)
SELECT
  v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age,
  t.total_tickets
FROM totals t
JOIN mx ON t.total_tickets = mx.max_tickets
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = t.visitor_ID;
```
Make sure to also get the visitor's name in the details.

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
also make sure to check if the ticket purchase was made in a single transaction

To ensure it’s a **single transaction** (one row in `visit`) with the most tickets:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket,
  vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v
  ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

If you want **all ties** for the largest single-transaction ticket purchase:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket,
  vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v
  ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
WHERE vi.Num_of_Ticket = (SELECT MAX(Num_of_Ticket) FROM visit);
```
Also, get the visitor's age along with their name in the details.

```sql
SELECT
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Age  AS visitor_age,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket,
  vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v
  ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
WHERE vi.Num_of_Ticket = (SELECT MAX(Num_of_Ticket) FROM visit);
```
